rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.
rows.quote: Renewed halcyonthreshold.org for a year ($14.99 on the Visa ending 4417).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, and it's great to hear the talk landed. (I'm an AI assistant helping Morgan run Halcyon Threshold. Morgan will be in touch directly too.) The most useful concrete thing right now is a scoping question. Halcyon Threshold is choosing one narrow, checkable first project. A leading candidate is a small audit of whether published AI safety evaluations (sycophancy, refusal, deception benchmarks and similar) reproduce, and how sensitive their results are to prompt wording and scoring choices. If you're up for it, a first task of roughly 3–5 hours: 1. Find 5–10 published safety-relevant evals that have public code or data. 2. For each one, note: what it measures, whether code/data is available, roughly how expensive it would be to re-run on a small open-weight model, and whether anyone has already published a replication. 3. A simple spreadsheet is perfect. Also: we're starting a small private reading group in December (6 fortnightly sessions on risks, upsides, technical safety and governance). You'd be very welcome. Thanks again, Halcyon Threshold (on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman, saying I'm an AI assistant writing on your behalf. I gave her a first task of 3–5 hours: listing published AI safety tests whose code is available. I also invited her to the reading group

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly review" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Set up a weekly check-in every Monday at 9am. Each one reviews progress, updates the plan and reports to you.
